results.input: AppLixir rewarded web advertising and publishers

output.checklist:
1. Obtain written confirmation from AppLixir of current publisher eligibility, traffic minimum, prohibited-content rules, treatment of AI-generated/mature content, child-directed traffic, consent requirements, payout terms, and applicable TCF version. 
2. Register the production and staging domains, complete ownership/traffic disclosures, and retain approval evidence. 
3. Integrate the current SDK version from official documentation; use sandbox/test keys and a real HTTPS staging domain for full-fidelity testing. 
4. Implement opt-in Watch Ad UX with visible reward terms, frequency caps, cooldowns, first-session protection, and `noAd`/error fallbacks. 
5. Grant rewards only after verified server-side callback processing; validate signatures, enforce nonce/idempotency and replay protection, bind rewards to the authenticated user/session, and log audit events. 
6. Publish and validate `ads.txt`, configure consent/CMP behavior by geography, document privacy notices, retention, deletion, and any PPID/user-ID handling. 
7. Add automated moderation and human escalation for AI-generated content; prevent restricted mature content from entering ad-supported placements and maintain age/parental controls where relevant. 
8. Separate ad rewards from subscriptions and paid packs; prohibit accidental purchase substitution, disclose limitations, and measure cannibalization. 
9. Instrument requests, impressions, completions, no-ad/error rates, eCPM, ARPDAU, geography, retention, support complaints, refunds, and invalid-traffic adjustments. 
10. Run a 2–4 week controlled pilot across geographies and cohorts; label AppLixir’s CPM/fill/revenue claims Uncertain until SynapticGM’s own data validates them. 
11. Before any mobile-store wrapper or native release, separately verify Apple/Google advertising, payments, age-rating, privacy, and user-generated/AI-content rules; do not assume web approval transfers to stores. 
12. Include creator marketing safeguards: disclose sponsored/reward mechanics, prohibit deceptive “free” claims, and moderate creator-promoted mature or prohibited experiences.
output.confirmed_facts: AppLixir presents a web-first rewarded-video platform for HTML5, React, vanilla JavaScript, Unity WebGL, Cocos, WordPress, iOS, and Android; its support site documents a v6 JavaScript SDK using `initializeAndOpenPlayer`, `preloadAd()`, completion callbacks, sandbox keys, and server-to-server callbacks with an MD5 signature, with the server webhook treated as the reward source of truth [1] [2]. Publisher onboarding requires a live, publicly accessible, original, policy-compliant site; the FAQ states review is typically 1–2 business days and identifies misleading, adult, and crypto-related content as rejection risks [2] [3]. Approved publishers must integrate the SDK, test serving, and publish AppLixir entries in `ads.txt`; payment is described as Net-30 after month-end with a standard $100 threshold, and payment/transaction fees may be deducted [2]. AppLixir advertises built-in GDPR/TCF consent handling, CCPA support, geo-detection, reporting by geography/site, and invalid-traffic filtering [1] [2]. Its official pages claim typical rewarded-video CPMs of $4–15 or $8–15, 30–40% engagement, 85–95% fill, and 2–3 ads per engaged user, but these are vendor marketing estimates rather than guaranteed benchmarks; the homepage also contains inconsistent thresholds and compliance-version wording (100,000 monthly impressions versus the FAQ’s 5,000 daily impressions/active users, and TCF 2.2 versus TCF 2.3), so SynapticGM must confirm current commercial and policy terms directly with AppLixir before launch [1] [2]. No official AppLixir page reviewed establishes a child-directed/ COPPA-specific product mode, an approval rule for mature AI-generated interactive content, or a subscription/pack billing capability; those areas require separate legal, platform, and vendor review.
output.operational_implications: Use AppLixir as an optional web reward layer for clearly defined, non-cash benefits such as temporary access, extra generation credits, or cosmetic/content unlocks; make reward entitlement server-authoritative with signed S2S reconciliation and idempotency; gate ad prompts behind explicit user choice, preload availability, cooldowns, and graceful no-ad fallbacks; keep mature or sexually explicit/otherwise restricted AI content outside ad-supported surfaces until AppLixir gives written eligibility guidance, and provide age/consent controls; model revenue using conservative experiments rather than published CPM/fill claims, while separately monetizing subscriptions and packs through a compliant checkout and testing ad impact on retention and conversion
output.risks: The principal release risk is policy ambiguity: AppLixir explicitly flags adult and misleading content, while SynapticGM’s AI-generated interactive output can vary dynamically and may cross restricted-content boundaries. A child-directed or family audience may trigger additional consent, age-assurance, advertising, and platform requirements that AppLixir’s reviewed materials do not expressly solve. Client-only reward granting is vulnerable to spoofing, replay, double-crediting, and manipulated callbacks; low fill, geo/device variance, invalid-traffic deductions, browser privacy controls, and ad-blocking can materially reduce yield. Published CPM, engagement, fill, and revenue figures are uncertain estimates, not guarantees. Conflicting official onboarding thresholds and TCF version statements should be treated as a launch blocker until confirmed in the publisher agreement or support ticket.

results.input: Google AdMob rewarded ads plus Families and Google Play policies

output.checklist:
1. Decide and document an adult-only versus mixed-audience product boundary; add age assurance/neutral age screening where applicable and prevent minors from mature experiences.
2. Build an AI safety pipeline: prompt/output filters, sexual/minor exploitation and abuse prevention, self-harm/illegal/deceptive-content controls, user report/flag action in-app, moderation queue, audit logs, appeals, and abuse-response SLAs.
3. Define rewarded rewards as non-transferable platform utility only; publish reward amount, action, bundle count, random odds and all possible outcomes before opt-in, with a functional skip/dismiss route.
4. Integrate server-side verification for ad rewards; make callbacks authenticated, replay-resistant and idempotent, and reconcile client, server, impression and ledger events.
5. Use Google test ad IDs in development/staging, separate production identifiers, and prohibit staff self-clicks, click incentives, bot traffic, forced ad interactions and creator messaging that encourages clicks.
6. Implement consent and privacy controls for EEA/UK and other applicable jurisdictions, accurately map every SDK/API data flow, use non-personalized/child-safe ad treatment where required, and publish an accurate privacy policy.
7. For Android, complete Play target-audience/content, IARC rating, Data safety, permissions, app-access/reviewer credentials, ads and in-app-purchase declarations; ensure store metadata and creator claims are accurate and non-spammy.
8. Integrate Play Billing 8+ for Android digital subscriptions/packs/ad-free features, verify purchases on a secure backend, process refunds/revocations, and consume real-time developer notifications; request the stated deadline extension if needed.
9. Maintain a single entitlement service with platform-specific receipt verification, SKU/versioning, restore flows, grace periods, cancellation handling and web-to-mobile account linking that does not bypass Play rules.
10. Run staged experiments for rewarded-ad opt-in, completion, fill, consent rate, retention, ARPDAU and creator cohorts by country/device; report finalized earnings and fraud-adjusted net revenue. Treat all revenue benchmarks as Uncertain until validated.
output.confirmed_facts: Google AdMob rewarded ads may grant only indirect or non-monetary, non-transferable rewards usable within the publisher’s platform; cash, cryptocurrency, gift cards, and other direct monetary items are prohibited. Random rewards require advance disclosure of odds/possible outcomes. The reward and required action must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed before each ad; ordinary rewarded ads require affirmative opt-in, must be skippable/dismissible without impairing normal use, and the promised reward must be delivered. Google documents server-side verification for validating rewarded views, and its Android guidance requires test ad-unit IDs during development because live test traffic can lead to suspension; rewarded ads are an Android SDK capability, not a generic web entitlement. [1] [2] [3] AdMob treats self-clicks, repeated clicks/impressions, incentivized clicks, bots, and deceptive traffic as invalid; Google can limit, suspend, or disable ad serving/account, and the publisher remains responsible even for third-party sabotage. [2] For children or mixed-audience Play apps, developers must accurately declare target ages, content ratings, Data safety, and Families answers; child-directed experiences require child-appropriate content, approved SDKs, non-personalized advertising, and a neutral age screen for mixed audiences, with restrictions on identifiers and sensitive data. [4] AI-generated-content apps must prevent restricted content and provide in-app reporting/flagging so user reports inform filtering and moderation. [5] Digital subscriptions, virtual currency, extra playtime, add-ons, features, and ad-free functionality distributed in a Play app generally require Google Play Billing; secure backend purchase verification, entitlement management, and real-time subscription notifications are recommended, and new apps/updates must use Billing Library 8+ by Aug 31, 2026 unless an extension is obtained. [6] [7] Google’s official materials do not provide a dependable universal rewarded-ad eCPM or revenue benchmark; any forecast is Uncertain and must be tested by geography, platform, consent status, fill, retention, and fraud-adjusted finalized earnings.
output.operational_implications: Keep rewarded currency strictly platform-bound, non-transferable, and non-cashable, with explicit opt-in, reward copy, skip path, and fulfillment ledger; treat web and Android monetization as separate integrations because the cited rewarded-ad implementation is SDK-based, while web monetization needs a separately approved Google web product and policy review; launch mature AI roleplay as adult/age-gated rather than child/family-targeted unless every accessible output, SDK, ad treatment, and data flow satisfies Families requirements; implement server-side AdMob SSV plus idempotent reward grants, rate limits, anomaly detection, and purchase verification before scaling creator traffic; use Play Billing for Android digital packs/subscriptions and maintain a platform-neutral entitlement backend, while measuring revenue experimentally instead of relying on non-official benchmarks
output.risks: The largest release risk is product ambiguity: an open-ended AI GM can generate sexual, exploitative, violent, deceptive, or otherwise restricted content, and Play requires prevention plus in-app reporting; mature content combined with child reach or inaccurate target-audience declarations can trigger rejection, removal, or suspension. Reward loops that resemble cash, transferable value, forced viewing, misleading calls to click, or rewards granted solely from client callbacks create AdMob policy and fraud exposure. Creator campaigns can also produce invalid or low-quality traffic; Google places responsibility on the publisher even when a third party causes invalid activity. Privacy/consent failures, unapproved SDKs, missing disclosures, or cross-platform entitlement mistakes can block launch. Revenue/eCPM estimates are Uncertain until controlled tests produce finalized, fraud-adjusted results.
output.topic: Google AdMob and Google Play launch readiness for SynapticGM

results.input: AppLovin MAX and ironSource mediation plus Unity Ads rewarded inventory

1. Decide whether rewarded ads launch in a native mobile app, a mobile wrapper, or a separate web-compatible demand product; do not assume MAX/LevelPlay SDK inventory works directly in the browser.
2. Obtain publisher approvals, create app/store records, configure placements, and verify supported SDK/adapters for the target Android and iOS versions.
3. Publish and maintain a public privacy policy naming ad/mediation providers; implement CMP flows and pass GDPR/UK/Swiss and applicable U.S. opt-out signals before SDK initialization.
4. Define and enforce a child/age policy: exclude users who qualify as children from AppLovin, avoid child-directed positioning, document age signals, and validate Unity/LevelPlay age-restricted settings.
5. Build an AI moderation gate covering sexual and suggestive content, synthetic sexual content, graphic violence, hate, illegal activity, self-harm/unsafe content, scams, malware, IP infringement, and significant unmoderated UGC; add report, block, takedown, appeal, and audit workflows.
6. Use app-ads.txt where applicable, keep seller authorization current, and monitor invalid-traffic and fraud signals; never buy incentivized or artificial traffic.
7. Implement server-side reward ledgers with nonce/idempotency, completion verification, replay protection, per-user/device/IP velocity limits, chargeback/reversal handling, and observability for callback anomalies.
8. Keep rewards optional and clearly disclosed; test that ads do not gate core safety, account recovery, paid entitlements, or promised subscription benefits.
9. Run geography/platform/consent A-B tests for fill, eCPM, completion, latency, crashes, retention, creator conversion, and net revenue; label all forecasts Uncertain until statistically sufficient results exist.
10. Complete Google Play/App Store privacy, age-rating, data-safety, tracking, payment, and content declarations for the final binary, and re-check network policies at each SDK or policy update.
output.confirmed_facts: AppLovin’s publisher policy, updated June 18, 2026, requires substantive original content, user engagement, legal/privacy compliance, and moderation/reporting controls for significant user-generated content; it prohibits monetizing sexually explicit/adult content, graphic violence, hateful or unsafe content, scams, malware, IP infringement, and fraudulent traffic, while reserving case-by-case review and enforcement [1]. AppLovin’s MAX privacy guidance makes the publisher responsible for obtaining consent and passing consent/Do Not Sell and other jurisdictional flags before SDK initialization; it expressly prohibits using AppLovin services with children or child-directed apps, including mixed-audience users who qualify as children under applicable law [2]. Unity LevelPlay supports user-initiated full-screen rewarded ads in exchange for in-app rewards, with placement configuration, reward callbacks, pacing/capping and mediation across multiple networks; Unity’s official integration is SDK/app oriented rather than a generic web-ad product [3] [4]. Unity’s app-ads.txt documentation describes the IAB authorization mechanism for reducing invalid traffic and verifying legitimate sellers [5]. Unity’s Advertising and Monetization Services Content Policy, updated June 30, 2026, prohibits deceptive, illegal, graphic, hateful, profane and sexually explicit or suggestive content, and expressly prohibits synthetic, manipulated, or AI-generated sexual content; Unity may reject/remove content at its discretion [6]. Unity’s current privacy guidance requires age-restricted status and consent handling before initializing relevant ad SDKs, and LevelPlay can pass consent to supported networks, subject to network-specific support and configuration [7] [8]. No official source reviewed supplies a reliable universal eCPM, fill-rate, or revenue benchmark; any such number for SynapticGM is Uncertain and must be measured by geography, platform, consent state, placement, demand mix, and retention cohort.
output.operational_implications: Treat MAX and LevelPlay/Unity Ads as mobile-app monetization tracks, not a drop-in web-first solution; plan a native wrapper or mobile client and keep web rewards behind a separate, policy-reviewed web ad product; make SynapticGM’s AI-content pipeline enforce hard blocks for sexual/suggestive content, synthetic sexual content, graphic violence, hate, illegal activity, IP misuse, scams, and unsafe user-generated material before an ad is shown; implement age gating/age assurance, child exclusion, CMP consent, regional opt-out signals, privacy disclosures, and SDK initialization only after required signals are set; make rewarded grants server-authoritative, idempotent, capped and tied to verified completion callbacks, then test mediation waterfalls, fill, latency, completion, fraud, retention and net revenue before pricing subscriptions or packs
output.risks: The largest release risk is product-policy mismatch: an AI GM can generate unpredictable user/creator content, and AppLovin’s child prohibition is especially restrictive because it disallows SDK use for qualifying children even in mixed or general-audience apps. Unity likewise retains broad rejection/removal discretion and bans AI-generated sexual content. Reward spoofing, replayed callbacks, device farms, VPN/geo anomalies, invalid traffic, consent-state errors, SDK/ad-network version drift, and app-store privacy disclosures can cause clawbacks, disabled demand, or store rejection. A web-first launch may not qualify for the mobile SDK inventory described in the official documentation. Subscription/pack economics and ad-revenue benchmarks remain Uncertain until controlled tests produce SynapticGM-specific data.
output.topic: AppLovin MAX, ironSource LevelPlay, and Unity Ads rewarded-ad readiness

results.input: Apple App Store policies for AI-generated content, mature content, subscriptions, and advertising

output.checklist:
1. Define SynapticGM’s target age rating, mature-content taxonomy, declared-age/verified-age controls, and child-directed exclusion policy before App Store metadata is finalized.
2. Add pre-publication and post-publication AI/creator moderation, prompt/output filters, human escalation, report and block tools, published support contact, audit trails, and deletion/takedown SLAs.
3. Ensure NSFW or above-rating content is hidden by default in iOS and can only be accessed through an age-restricted flow consistent with Apple’s creator-content rules.
4. Build a native iOS experience with meaningful platform-specific value; document all remote chatbot, streaming, HTML5, or creator functionality and ensure it cannot bypass privacy, moderation, age, or payment controls.
5. Configure StoreKit products for subscriptions, consumable credits/packs, restore purchases, upgrades/downgrades, server-side transaction verification, App Store Server Notifications, and entitlement reconciliation with the web.
6. Make all IAP products visible and functional in the review build; provide a complete demo account or full-featured demo mode, live backend, test credentials, and detailed App Review notes.
7. Implement privacy policy links, consent and withdrawal flows, account deletion, data retention/deletion controls, AI-provider disclosures, data minimization, ATT where tracking occurs, and a complete third-party SDK/data inventory.
8. Select an ad network whose SDK, targeting, consent, age signals, creative controls, and child-safe documentation meet Apple requirements; ensure rewarded ads never require tracking permission or system permissions and cannot be farmed.
9. Instrument rewarded-ad experiments for fill rate, eCPM, reward cost, session length, retention, conversion, fraud rate, refunds, and incremental revenue by geo/device/age/consent segment; label all forecasts Uncertain until tested.
10. Prepare accurate age-rating answers, 4+-appropriate screenshots/icons/previews, privacy metadata, subscription disclosures, creator-content disclosures, and custom product pages for compliant creator marketing.
11. Test review-critical paths on supported iPhone/iPad devices, IPv6-only networks, poor connectivity, purchase restoration, account deletion, moderation escalation, age restrictions, and ad failure states.
12. Run a pre-submission legal and policy review for copyright/trademark rights in generated and creator content, children’s privacy laws, mature-content distribution, payments, and every launch storefront.
output.confirmed_facts: Apple’s App Review Guidelines (last updated June 8, 2026) prohibit overtly sexual or pornographic material and require AI/creator/user-generated content to be filtered, reportable, blockable, supported by published contact information, and actively removed when it violates policy [1](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/). Creator-content apps must identify content exceeding the app’s age rating and use verified or declared-age restrictions; web-sourced incidental mature NSFW content must be hidden by default and enabled on the website [1]. Apple permits HTML5/JavaScript mini apps, streaming games, chatbots, and plug-ins, but requires the host app to apply privacy, UGC moderation, age-rating, and payment rules to that software [1]. Digital content, subscriptions, credits, gems, and in-app consumables generally require In-App Purchase; multiplatform apps may let users access web-acquired content or consumables only if the same items are also available as in-app purchases [1]. Subscriptions must clearly disclose what is included and the price, work across the user’s Apple devices, and deliver value without requiring social posting or other promotional tasks [1]. Ads must be age-appropriate, cannot artificially inflate impressions or clicks, and an app cannot be predominantly an ad display; Apple remains responsible for the overall app experience including ad networks and SDKs [1]. Kids Category apps require a parental gate for links and purchases, generally prohibit third-party advertising and analytics, and allow only limited contextual advertising with publicly documented child-safe practices and human review of creatives [1]. All apps need an accessible privacy policy in App Store Connect and in-app, consent and withdrawal mechanisms for collected usage data, data minimization, account deletion when account creation is supported, explicit disclosure and permission for sharing with third-party AI, and App Tracking Transparency consent for tracking [1]. App Review requires a complete, stable build, accurate metadata and age rating, live backend services, reviewer access or a full demo mode, and detailed review notes for non-obvious features and purchases [1]. A native iOS app that is merely a repackaged website may be rejected; Apple expects app-specific utility and functionality [1]. Apple provides StoreKit APIs for auto-renewable subscriptions and App Store Connect tools for pricing and management [2](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/), while custom product pages can target different audiences and campaigns through unique URLs [3](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/product-page/). No reliable official Apple benchmark establishes rewarded-ad revenue; any eCPM, fill-rate, retention, or ARPDAU estimate is Uncertain and must be measured by SynapticGM’s own geo/device/age-segment experiments.
output.operational_implications: Launch web-first with mature AI-generated interactive content controlled by server-side moderation, hidden-by-default NSFW settings, age gates, reporting, blocking, audit logs, and rapid takedown workflows; treat the iOS client as a curated native product rather than a thin web wrapper, with a stable offline/online review path and reviewer demo mode; implement StoreKit for subscriptions and credit/pack purchases in iOS, while synchronizing entitlements with the web and ensuring web-purchased digital goods are also purchasable in-app; keep rewarded ads optional and non-coercive, never require tracking or notification permissions for rewards, use age-rating-safe creatives, prevent repeat/impression/click manipulation, and exclude child-directed cohorts or use a documented contextual child-safe network; build privacy controls covering AI-provider disclosure, consent, ATT, retention, deletion, minimization, and third-party SDK governance; use App Store custom product pages, creator campaigns, and deep links for segmented marketing, but avoid misleading metadata, paid-review manipulation, forced ratings, or promotional content that exceeds the app’s declared rating
output.risks: The highest release risk is uncontrolled AI or creator output drifting into pornography, exploitation, targeted abuse, threats, hateful content, or content above the declared age rating; Apple can remove noncompliant UGC services and, for egregious or repeated failures, the app and developer account. A thin iOS wrapper may fail the minimum-functionality rule, while server-driven chatbot or mini-game content still remains the developer’s responsibility. Subscription bait-and-switch, unclear entitlements, missing IAP visibility, failed restore/synchronization, or web-only digital purchase flows can cause rejection. Ad-network SDK behavior, tracking, child data handling, and creative review create privacy and Kids Category exposure. Fraud risks include reward farming, device/account emulation, chargebacks, refund abuse, click/impression inflation, and creator campaigns that manipulate App Store discovery. Advertising revenue benchmarks are Uncertain because Apple does not publish a universal rewarded-ad eCPM benchmark; test by geography, platform, consent status, age cohort, placement, frequency cap, and retention impact before committing to revenue targets.
output.topic: Apple App Store launch readiness for SynapticGM

results.input: Stripe Billing subscriptions payment webhooks and UK digital service consumer requirements

output.checklist:
1. Create a product/compliance matrix defining age audience, mature-content boundaries, prohibited generations, geographic availability, and whether the service is likely to be accessed by children.
2. Publish UK-ready terms, privacy notice, refund/cancellation policy, business identity/contact details, tax-inclusive prices, billing period, renewal/cancellation conditions, and digital-content functionality before checkout; obtain legally appropriate express consent before immediate digital supply where cancellation rights are affected.
3. Implement Stripe Checkout/Billing, customer portal or equivalent cancellation path, PaymentIntent/Invoice/Subscription event handling, signature verification, idempotency, replay protection, audit logs, and a fast 2xx webhook response.
4. Model entitlement states for active, trial, past_due, unpaid, canceled, incomplete, refunded, disputed, and chargeback conditions; reconcile periodically against Stripe and revoke or quarantine benefits safely.
5. Keep packs non-transferable unless deliberately designed otherwise; prevent client-side currency manipulation, replayed ad rewards, multi-account farming, coupon abuse, card testing, and velocity anomalies using server-side ledgers and fraud controls.
6. For rewarded ads, show an unambiguous opt-in and reward description, allow skip/dismissal without blocking ordinary use, prohibit cash-like rewards, deliver only after verified completion, and record ad-network callbacks for reconciliation.
7. Complete a UK GDPR/Children’s Code DPIA covering age estimation or gating, AI prompts and transcripts, profiling, advertising, analytics, creator data, retention, deletion, parental controls, and vendor sharing; default to high privacy where children may access the service.
8. Build AI safety controls: input/output moderation, sexual-content and exploitation blocks, self-harm and illegal-content handling, abuse reporting, creator takedown, human escalation, age labels, audit trails, and model/vendor incident response.
9. Before mobile publication, map every monetized feature to Apple/Google billing rules, complete age ratings and data-safety disclosures, verify Families/ad-SDK eligibility if relevant, and test UGC, chat, mature-content, and account-deletion review paths.
10. Treat ad economics as Uncertain until tested; run region/device/age-mode experiments measuring fill, eCPM, completion, reward cost, retention, subscription cannibalisation, consent loss, invalid traffic, and net contribution.
output.confirmed_facts: Stripe says subscription integrations require webhook destinations because much subscription activity is asynchronous; production endpoints must use HTTPS, verify Stripe signatures, return 2xx quickly, and handle payment failures and status changes such as trial-to-active transitions [1] [2]. Stripe supports subscription entitlements and customer self-service/cancellation flows, but SynapticGM must define fulfillment, failed-payment, grace-period, refund, and cancellation behavior in its own application [3] [4]. UK online sellers must disclose business identity/contact details, service description, tax-inclusive price, payment method, contract minimum/billing period, termination conditions, cancellation rights, and digital-content functionality before order; customers generally receive a 14-day cancellation right, with specific digital-download/streaming exceptions requiring compliant information and consent, and must receive a savable contract confirmation [5]. The ICO Children’s Code applies to online services likely to be accessed by children and sets 15 standards, including best interests, DPIA, age-appropriate application, high-privacy defaults, data minimisation, limited sharing, parental controls, and restrictions on profiling and nudges [6]. Google AdMob rewarded ads cannot grant cash, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or other direct monetary items; non-transferable in-platform rewards are permitted, with clear pre-disclosure, affirmative opt-in, no coercion, reward delivery, and server-side verification available [7] [8]. Google Play Families policies require Families-compliant ad SDKs and child-appropriate treatment where children or unknown-age users are targeted [9]. Apple’s App Review Guidelines require safe, functional apps and impose additional requirements on user-generated content, in-app purchases/subscriptions, privacy, and objectionable or mature content; any future mobile build must pass the applicable age-rating and content-review process [10] [11]. These are policy summaries, not legal advice; counsel should validate UK consumer, privacy, age-assurance, tax, and content classification decisions.
output.operational_implications: Use Stripe Checkout/Billing plus a signed, idempotent HTTPS webhook service as the sole source of truth for entitlements; separate subscription benefits from consumable packs and implement explicit refund, cancellation, grace, and chargeback states; launch web-first with clear UK pricing, terms, cancellation/withdrawal handling, digital-content consent, and durable order confirmations; make rewarded ads optional and grant only non-transferable SynapticGM credits/content, with pre-ad disclosure, completion callbacks, server-side validation, frequency caps, and no ads in mature or child-directed contexts; choose and enforce an age/content policy early—family-safe mode with high privacy and child safeguards, or an adults-oriented product with reliable gating, moderation, reporting, provenance, and app-store-ready content controls
output.risks: The highest risks are granting premium content from an unverified client-side payment or ad callback, duplicate or out-of-order webhooks, entitlement leakage after failed renewal or chargeback, misleading recurring-price or cancellation UX, and unlawful digital-content withdrawal handling. A mixed-audience AI GM may be treated as likely accessed by children even if not intended for them, triggering Children’s Code design obligations; profiling, personalised advertising, nudges, chat logs, location, and creator analytics require documented purpose limitation and minimisation. Mature or sexual AI-generated scenarios, anonymous/user-generated chat, unsafe outputs, and inadequate moderation can cause payment-provider, ad-network, app-store, and reputational rejection. Advertising revenue benchmarks are Uncertain and not reliably established by the cited official policies; test fill rate, eCPM, reward conversion, retention impact, regional consent rates, and fraud-adjusted net revenue with controlled experiments rather than planning from generic benchmarks.
output.topic: SynapticGM payments, consumer compliance, ads, and launch readiness

results.input: UK ICO Age Appropriate Design Code, UK GDPR, and children online privacy requirements

output.checklist:
1. Decide and document whether SynapticGM is adult-only or child-accessible in the UK; align product copy, creator campaigns, SEO, age gate, and access controls, and test the restriction in practice.
2. Complete and approve a child-focused DPIA before launch; include AI generation, prompts, memory, moderation, profiling, rewarded ads, cookies, payments, fraud signals, analytics, vendors, international transfers, retention, and deletion.
3. Create an age-assurance design with risk rationale, data minimisation, spoofing/false-positive tests, escalation, parental-authority verification where under-13 consent is used, and a plan to apply Code protections to uncertain-age users.
4. Implement high-privacy defaults: private profiles, no public location, geolocation off, minimal telemetry, short retention, restricted data sharing, separate purposes, child-readable notices, and accessible rights/deletion tools.
5. Disable behavioural advertising and profiling by default for child modes; use contextual rewarded ads, obtain PECR consent for non-essential cookies, record consent, honour withdrawal, and prevent ad SDKs from collecting child identifiers.
6. Define mature-content policy and technical enforcement: age-banded generation, prompt/output filters, human escalation, blocklists, audit logs, report-and-remove, crisis/self-harm and sexual-content handling, and no mature content in child mode.
7. Review subscriptions, packs, virtual currency, reward claims, cancellation, renewal, parental controls, purchase confirmations, and marketing copy for unfair pressure, dark patterns, and child-directed inducement.
8. Map every processor and subprocessor, sign appropriate data-processing terms, verify model/ad/payment vendor use of data, UK transfer mechanisms, breach response, security, and deletion on request.
9. Build fraud prevention with documented necessity and proportionality; cap rewarded-ad frequency and rewards, detect automation/replay/multi-account abuse, provide appeals, and avoid retaining raw identifiers longer than needed.
10. Obtain legal/privacy and child-safety sign-off, retain DPIA and age-assurance evidence, and re-review after material feature, vendor, AI-model, advertising, or UK-law changes.
11. Treat revenue assumptions as Uncertain; A/B test consented versus contextual inventory, fill, eCPM, reward cost, retention, payer conversion, refund rate, fraud loss, and child/adult cohort performance without using children’s data for behavioural optimisation.
12. Before creator marketing, review audience composition, disclosures, age targeting, direct-marketing permissions, influencer contracts, moderation obligations, and claims about safety, AI capability, or earnings.
output.confirmed_facts: The ICO Children’s Code is a statutory code of practice comprising 15 flexible standards for information-society services likely to be accessed by children under 18, including games and websites; it applies to UK and non-UK providers processing UK children’s data [1]. It requires the child’s best interests to be a primary consideration, a pre-launch child-focused DPIA, age-appropriate transparency, high-privacy defaults, data minimisation, limited sharing, geolocation off by default, parental controls, and restrictions on nudging. If relying on consent for an online service offered directly to a child, UK GDPR Article 8 permits a child’s own consent from age 13; under 13 requires reasonable efforts to verify parental-authority consent [2]. The ICO says online services likely to be accessed by children are high-risk for DPIA purposes, especially where processing involves marketing, profiling, tracking, innovative AI, inferred data, or risks of harmful content [3]. Profiling, including behavioural advertising, should be off by default for children, separately controlled, and protected against harmful effects; non-essential cookies require prior PECR consent, in addition to a lawful basis for underlying processing [4]. The ICO’s age-assurance opinion recommends either applying the Code proportionately to all users or using age assurance proportionate to processing risk; self-declaration alone is not appropriate for high-risk services, and the guidance is currently under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 [5]. Children retain UK GDPR rights, including access, erasure, objection to direct-marketing profiling, and understandable privacy information. Direct marketing to children has significant potential for harm and must be assessed with other applicable advertising rules [6]. No reliable official benchmark establishes rewarded-ad revenue per user; any eCPM, fill-rate, conversion, or subscription uplift figures are Uncertain and must be tested by geography, age cohort, consent state, device, and ad format.
output.operational_implications: Treat SynapticGM as likely in scope of the Children’s Code if UK children could reasonably access the web-first game, even if adults are the target; either enforce a defensible 18+ restriction or apply child-safe protections broadly; separate child/adult or age-band modes before enabling mature AI-generated interactive content, and prohibit sexual, exploitative, self-harm, or otherwise age-inappropriate outputs for child modes; launch rewarded ads only with contextual/non-personalised delivery for children, no behavioural profiling by default, no non-essential tracking without PECR consent, clear opt-in/out and no manipulative reward prompts; make subscriptions and packs transparent, avoid child-directed pressure or scarcity nudges, provide parental controls/refunds/support pathways, and minimise payment and purchase data; complete a DPIA covering AI prompts/outputs, inferred data, moderation, age assurance, ads, fraud telemetry, processors, retention, international transfers, and creator marketing before launch.

Combining gameplay telemetry, prompt history, inferred interests, rewarded-ad eligibility, and creator audiences can become profiling or invisible processing. AI-generated content can create child-safety, privacy, bias, copyright, and harmful-content exposure risks even where the model provider is a processor. Fraud controls must be narrowly designed: device fingerprints, IP data, payment identifiers, and anti-abuse scores are personal data and need necessity, transparency, retention limits, access controls, and a lawful basis. Non-compliant cookies, consent, direct marketing, dark patterns, or purchase flows can delay web launch and create enforcement, platform, advertiser, and reputational risk. 1. Classify SynapticGM by intended audience, actual audience, child-directed signals, age bands, and mature-content modes; obtain counsel review for US COPPA/FTC and UK CAP/DMCCA exposure.

output.confirmed_facts: FTC Endorsement Guides require endorsements to be honest and non-misleading; a material connection that consumers would not reasonably expect—such as payment, free access, affiliate commission, employment, or other value—must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, and advertisers share responsibility for what endorsers say. The FTC says disclosures should be hard to miss, understandable, and made in the content itself; the Guides are not a safe harbor and claims require substantiation [1][2]. COPPA covers child-directed websites/apps and general-audience services with actual knowledge of collecting personal information from under-13s, including identifiers, persistent identifiers, voice/video, and geolocation; covered operators need a clear privacy policy, direct notice and verifiable parental consent (with limited exceptions), parental access/deletion controls, security, data minimization, retention limits, and cannot condition participation on unnecessary data. The FTC’s 2025 COPPA amendment is the current rule and includes stronger controls around third-party disclosures/advertising, so SynapticGM should verify the final text and effective dates before launch [3][4]. The FTC’s amended recurring-subscriptions rule applies broadly to automatic renewals and free trials: disclose material terms before enrollment, obtain and retain proof of consent for at least three years, and provide cancellation that is as easy as signup and available through the same medium; other state laws may add requirements [5]. In the UK, CAP Code section 2 requires marketing communications to be obviously identifiable. ASA/CAP guidance says paid, incentivized, affiliate, gifted, employee, ownership, and other commercially connected influencer content needs a prominent upfront label—preferably “Ad”—that is visible before engagement, not buried in hashtags, a bio, “see more,” poor contrast, or platform-dependent UI; brands and influencers are both responsible, including for virtual personas [6][7]. CAP’s children guidance defines children as under 16, requires immediate ad recognition, prohibits exploiting credulity/vulnerability, direct purchase appeals or pressure, and warns against harmful, distressing, violent, sexualized, or offensive material in insufficiently targeted media; under-12 immersive/integrated marketing needs enhanced disclosure. CAP’s age-targeting restrictions vary by product, with a 25% audience threshold for several restricted categories [8]. Neither FTC nor ASA publishes a dependable universal rewarded-ad revenue benchmark; any eCPM, completion, retention, conversion, or subscription uplift number should therefore be treated as Uncertain and validated by SynapticGM’s own geo/device/age-segment experiments.
output.operational_implications: Use an in-content, platform-safe “Ad”/“Paid partnership” disclosure template and contractually require creator compliance; keep creator claims limited to substantiated, reproducible gameplay/product experiences and audit posts; launch with age assurance, child-directedness classification, parental-consent/data controls, no targeted third-party ads for child users unless legally supported, and separate mature-content experiences from family acquisition; make rewarded ads opt-in, clearly labeled, skippable where appropriate, never deceptively disguised as gameplay or necessary progress, and block unsafe ad categories/creative from minors; implement subscription/packs consent records, clear price/renewal/trial terms, same-channel cancellation, refund/support workflows, fraud/chargeback/device-abuse monitoring, privacy retention/deletion, and controlled revenue/retention experiments before scaling
output.risks: The largest risks are undisclosed paid or affiliate creator content, misleading claims about AI capabilities or player outcomes, and creator-generated mature/violent/sexual material reaching minors or appearing in family-safe placements. A virtual creator is still within ASA influencer guidance, and both brand and creator can be exposed. COPPA exposure can arise from child-directed design, actual knowledge, voice/chat or persistent identifiers, ad-network SDKs, analytics, or AI prompts containing children’s data. Reward loops that pressure children, obscure ad identity, or tie progress to viewing can create unfairness and platform/regulatory issues. Subscription failures include hidden renewals, inadequate consent evidence, and difficult cancellation. Fraud, invalid traffic, incentivized clicks, bots, chargebacks, coupon abuse, and fabricated creator attribution can corrupt ad benchmarks and payment economics. Advertising-revenue figures are Uncertain until tested with independent measurement, frequency caps, fill-rate/invalid-traffic controls, and cohort-level A/B tests.
